summary: Comprehensive integration testing of new Bulk Scheduling feature. Backend: 7/7 pytest tests pass (empty items 400, 200-item limit, unauth 401, happy path creates + persists as scheduled, partial invalid rows reported, past-time auto-published by APScheduler). Frontend: /bulk page loads via nav-bulk, Shared Defaults (title prefix, timezone, recurrence, caption, hashtags, platform chips) all functional, 'connect first' toast shown for offline platforms, Slot Template Interval+Count mode preview count updates live, build-template & build-multi generate correct rows, row edit/duplicate/delete/add-blank all work, submit calls POST /api/posts/bulk, success toast shows count, redirects to /calendar, and bulk posts appear in Publish Queue. CSV import populates preview table correctly. No blocking issues.

design_issues.screen: Bulk / any select with dynamic options
issues: React hydration warning in console: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>'. Caused by devtools instrumentation wrapping option text in a span (x-file-name attrs). Non-blocking but noisy; may confuse future debugging. Consider suppressing in prod build or refactoring dynamic-var wrapping for <option> children.

critical_code_review_comments: BulkScheduler.js is ~600 lines (below 700 threshold but close). Consider extracting SlotTemplateBlock and the preview table into their own files if more modes are added.

Bulk endpoint has no ownership check on media_ids — a user could reference another user's media_id in a bulk item and it'd be stored. Downstream _publish_post lookups may 404 harmlessly, but it's a defense-in-depth gap worth patching.

server.py bulk_create_posts uses `datetime.fromisoformat(item.scheduled_at.replace('Z','+00:00'))` for validation but stores the raw string; ISO strings without timezone will pass validation and then be lexicographically compared by the scheduler — could cause off-by-timezone auto-publish timing. Frontend already sends UTC ISO so it's fine in practice.
Frontend CSV parser is naive (no quoted-comma handling) as noted in code comments — acceptable for internal use, but flag if this becomes user-facing.

Bulk POST does not validate that platforms in each item are among the user's connected platforms; it just stores them. Publishing later will surface the failure per-platform (already tested). Consider a warning at bulk-create time so users see it before scheduling.

success_rate.backend: 100% (7/7 new bulk tests + prior 19 still green)

seed_data_creation: Created bulk posts with TEST_bulk_* and TEST_UI Bulk* titles in db.posts for user test-user-e2e; some auto-published by the scheduler during the test window.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run bulk tests with: `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<url> pytest /app/backend/tests/test_bulk.py -v -o addopts=''`. The scheduler test polls 70s for auto-publish. Frontend tests use session_token cookie. Multi-media tab shares slot-pattern controls with template tab (mode/pattern/interval state is unified).
